name: Performance
description: Display and gaming settings that can cause stutter or slowdowns on some PCs.

tweaks.name: Turn off Windows variable refresh rate
tweaks.summary: Fixes stutter and very low frame rates on the desktop and in windowed apps. Any GPU.
tweaks.description: Windows can apply variable refresh rate (G-SYNC, FreeSync, Adaptive-Sync) to DirectX 11 and 12 games that do not support it themselves. On some PCs this makes the desktop and windowed apps stutter, flicker or drop to very low frame rates, sometimes close to 1 fps. Turning it off fixes that. Games that support VRR themselves still use it. This is the Variable refresh rate switch in Settings > System > Display > Graphics, and works with any graphics card.
tweaks.goodToKnow: Settings only shows this switch when your monitor and driver support VRR. Other graphics settings stored in the same value, such as Optimizations for windowed games and Auto HDR, are kept as they are.
tweaks.undo: The whole DirectXUserGlobalSettings value is saved first. Undo puts back exactly what was there, or removes it if it did not exist.

tweaks.name: Turn off hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling
tweaks.summary: Stops Windows from letting the GPU schedule its own work. On some PCs this causes stutter, frame drops or very low fps. Needs a restart.
tweaks.description: Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling (HAGS) lets the graphics card schedule its own work instead of Windows doing it. On some PCs and drivers this causes stutter, frame drops or very low fps. Turning it off is the same as the Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling switch in Settings > System > Display > Graphics > Advanced graphics settings. This is separate from G-SYNC and from the Windows variable refresh rate switch. A restart is required for the change to take effect. Windows only shows the switch when your GPU and driver support it.
tweaks.goodToKnow: If the switch is missing in Settings, your GPU or driver may not support this. When the setting has never been changed, Windows leaves it off and this item shows as already off.
tweaks.undo: The old HwSchMode value is saved first. Undo puts it back, or removes it if it was not there.

tweaks.name: Turn off NVIDIA G-SYNC (driver setting)
tweaks.summary: Turns off G-SYNC in the NVIDIA driver for all apps. NVIDIA graphics cards only.
tweaks.description: Sets "Enable G-SYNC globally" in the NVIDIA driver's global 3D profile to off, the same setting as in NVIDIA Control Panel. This fixes flicker and stutter that some G-SYNC and G-SYNC Compatible monitors show on the desktop and in windowed apps. Games will not use G-SYNC either, so you may see tearing unless V-Sync is on. This is separate from the Windows variable refresh rate switch.
tweaks.goodToKnow: Shows "Not applicable" when no NVIDIA driver is installed. The change is made through the NVIDIA driver on this PC (nvapi64.dll), nothing is downloaded.
tweaks.undo: The old driver value is saved first. Undo puts it back, or removes the override so the driver default applies again.

tweaks.name: Turn off background game recording
tweaks.summary: Stops Game Bar from recording gameplay in the background.
tweaks.description: Turns off Game DVR, which keeps recording the last minutes of gameplay so you can save a clip. This frees some GPU and disk use while gaming. Xbox Game Bar still opens with Win+G.
